visuals.title: Quiz
visuals.text: Five questions. Answer along on the cards below the transcript, then hear Marco's answers.

quiz.pause_at: Pause here if you want to think it through

questions.q: Orbit sells 30 million shares at €10: 10 million new and 20 million from existing owners. How much does Orbit itself receive, before fees?
questions.explain: Only the new shares raise money for the company: 10m × €10 = €100m, the primary part. Taking the whole €300m, Sofia's slip, counts the sellers' money too.
questions.explain_at: Orbit only gets the money for the new shares

questions.q: What does a greenshoe let the underwriters do?

options.text: Sell extra shares, and buy them back if the price falls
Raise the offer price once the book is covered
Sell more shares at a higher price on day one
Buy shares from the founders at a discount

questions.explain: The banks sell up to 15% more than the base deal. If the price falls they buy shares in the market, supporting it; if it rises they buy the extra shares from the sellers through the option.
questions.explain_at: The banks sell up to fifteen percent more shares than the base deal

questions.q: Orbit sells 30 million shares at €10 and closes its first day at €12. How much was left on the table?
questions.explain: €2 a share the sellers could have had, on all 30 million shares sold: €60m. Counting only the 10 million new shares gives €20m.
questions.explain_at: Thirty million shares times two euros: sixty million left on the table

questions.q: Arm's price range was $47 to $51. It priced at $51 and closed its first day at $63.59. Roughly what was the first-day rise?
questions.explain: $63.59 ÷ $51 − 1 ≈ 25%, measured from the offer price. From the bottom of the range it looks like 35%; dividing the gain by the closing price gives 20%.
questions.explain_at: Up almost twenty-five percent, a value of about sixty-five billion

questions.q: EQT's 40.3% premium for Qiagen is measured against which price?

options.text: The close the day before the announcement
The three-month average up to October
The close before reports of buyer interest
The price at Qiagen's Nasdaq listing

questions.explain: The unaffected price: €33.15 at the close on 8 July 2026, the last trading day before reports of private equity interest. Yesterday's close, Sofia's guess, already carries bid hope.
questions.explain_at: Forty point three percent over the close of thirty-three euros and fifteen cents
